fullPassage:
Letters to Nature

Dear Tree,
Whenever I walk past you, your beautiful leaves bring a smile to my face. Whenever I stop in front of you and take a deep breath of fresh air, I appreciate the oxygen that you produce. Without you and all your friends, we humans wouldn't be able to get enough oxygen. By the way, I noticed that a family of birds has made a nest in your branches. It's so kind of you to provide them with a home. I hope that more people realize how important you and all the other trees are to the environment. Have a nice day!

Believe it or not, trees in Melbourne, Australia receive emails like this all the time. How is it possible that trees have email addresses? And why are people sending them messages?

The story behind these emails begins with Melbourne's Urban Forest Strategy plan, a response to Australia's millennium drought. This drought lasted from the late 1990s to 2010. By the time it ended, 40 percent of the city's 77,000 trees were in a state of declining health. Furthermore, the overall number of trees was decreasing.

As a result, the amount of shade provided by trees within the city, also known as canopy cover, decreased. The loss of canopy cover is a major threat to urban environments because it raises temperatures. Higher temperatures in cities can be dangerous for residents, as they increase the risk of heat exhaustion. They also lead to a rise in the use of air conditioning. This speeds up climate change by increasing energy consumption and greenhouse gas emissions.

Something had to be done to deal with the loss of Melbourne's trees. In 2012, the city government announced its Urban Forest Strategy plan. It set the ambitious goal of planting more than 3,000 trees every year for the next twenty years. The plan also involved the creation of an online map called the Urban Forest Visual.

This interactive map shows the location of every single tree in the city's parks and along its roads. It uses colors and symbols to indicate each tree's age and genus. Also, users can click on a tree to find out its species and even send it an email. At first, the "Email this tree" function had a specific purpose. It was designed to allow people to easily inform council workers about trees that were damaged or in poor health.

After the map was posted online, something unexpected happened. The trees started receiving thousands of emails, but many of them were not reports about damage or poor health. Instead, they were love letters, poems, greetings, and messages expressing appreciation for the trees. One person wrote, "I love the way the light shines on your leaves and how your branches hang so low. It is almost like you are trying to hug me." The tree mail phenomenon quickly spread, and people all over the world started sending messages.

A message that was sent all the way from Russia said, "When I read about this wonderful project, I was inspired to write to you, even though I live thousands of miles away. Although we are separated by a great distance, we share the same planet and the same environment. Perhaps one day we will meet. Until then, I hope you can stay healthy and strong."

The global popularity of the tree mail phenomenon reminds us that we are all connected to nature, and we are all involved in building a more sustainable world. Without collective action from people across the globe, we would have little hope of saving our planet for future generations.

Locally, the tree mail phenomenon has inspired many Melbourne residents to offer their own ideas about building an environmentally friendly urban environment. Some have even volunteered to measure trees and monitor animals for nature programs in the city.

Meanwhile, the Urban Forest Strategy's tree planting project has remained on track, and canopy cover is predicted to increase from 23 percent in 2012 to 40 percent by the year 2040. Melbourne's urban forest strategy will help keep the city cool. It will also allow residents to interact with nature and engage in outdoor activities every day. As a result, residents will be happier and healthier as they move toward a greener future.

questions.passage: Whenever I walk past you, your beautiful leaves ①<u>bring</u> a smile to my face. Whenever I stop in front of you and take a deep breath of fresh air, I appreciate the oxygen ②<u>that</u> you produce. Without you and all your friends, we humans wouldn't be able ③<u>getting</u> enough oxygen. It's so kind of you ④<u>to provide</u> them with a home.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: 우리 인간들은 충분한 산소를 얻을 수 없을 거야.
det.analysis: ✅ ①bring: 주어 leaves(복수)에 맞는 동사 원형으로 정상. ✅ ②that: 목적격 관계대명사로 oxygen을 선행사로 하여 정상. ❌ ③getting: 원문은 'be able to get'. 'be able to + 동사원형' 구문에서 to가 필요. getting(동명사)은 불가. ✅ ④to provide: 'It's kind of you to provide'에서 to부정사는 정상.
det.tip: be able to + V원형: ~할 수 있다. to 뒤에는 반드시 동사원형이 와야 한다.

questions.passage: Believe it or not, trees in Melbourne, Australia ①<u>receive</u> emails like this all the time. The story behind these emails begins with Melbourne's Urban Forest Strategy plan. This drought ②<u>was lasted</u> from the late 1990s to 2010. By the time it ended, 40 percent of the city's 77,000 trees ③<u>were</u> in a state of ④<u>declining</u> health.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: 이 가뭄은 1990년대 후반부터 2010년까지 계속되었다.
det.analysis: ✅ ①receive: trees(복수)에 맞는 동사 원형으로 정상. ❌ ②was lasted: last(계속되다)는 자동사이므로 수동태 불가. 원문은 'lasted'. ✅ ③were: 40 percent of trees(복수)에 맞는 동사로 정상. ✅ ④declining: 현재분사가 health를 수식. '악화되는 건강'으로 정상.
det.tip: last(계속되다)는 자동사: 수동태 불가. 'The drought lasted ~'(○) / 'was lasted'(×).

questions.passage: The loss of canopy cover is a major threat to urban environments because it ①<u>raises</u> temperatures. Higher temperatures in cities can be dangerous for residents, as they increase the risk of heat exhaustion. They also lead to a ②<u>rise</u> in the use of air conditioning. This speeds up climate change by ③<u>increase</u> energy consumption and greenhouse gas ④<u>emissions</u>.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: 에너지 소비와 온실가스 배출물을 증가시킴으로써.
det.analysis: ✅ ①raises: 주어 it(단수)에 맞는 3인칭 단수 동사로 정상. ✅ ②rise: 'a rise'에서 명사로 정상. ❌ ③increase: 전치사 by 뒤에는 동명사가 와야 함. 원문은 'by increasing'. ✅ ④emissions: 복수 명사로 정상.
det.tip: by + V-ing: ~함으로써. 전치사 뒤에는 동명사(V-ing)가 와야 한다.

questions.passage: This interactive map shows the location of every single tree in the city's parks. It uses colors and symbols to indicate each tree's age and genus. Also, users can click on a tree ①<u>to find</u> out its species. At first, the function had a specific purpose. It was designed to allow people ②<u>to easily inform</u> council workers about trees ③<u>that</u> were damaged or in poor health. After the map was posted online, something ④<u>unexpecting</u> happened.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: 지도가 온라인에 게재된 후, 예상 밖의 일이 일어났다.
det.analysis: ✅ ①to find: 목적을 나타내는 부정사로 정상. ✅ ②to easily inform: allow + O + to V에서 부사 easily 삽입으로 정상. ✅ ③that: trees를 선행사로 하는 주격 관계대명사로 정상. ❌ ④unexpecting: 원문은 'unexpected'. something을 수식하는 과거분사(-ed). unexpecting은 존재하지 않는 단어. '예상되지 않은' → unexpected.
det.tip: unexpected(예상 밖의): 과거분사가 형용사로 쓰임. something unexpected처럼 -thing 뒤에 형용사가 후치수식.

questions.passage: Instead, they were love letters, poems, greetings, and messages expressing ①<u>appreciation</u> for the trees. One person wrote, "I love the way the light shines on your leaves and how your branches hang so ②<u>low</u>. It is almost like you are trying to hug me." The tree mail phenomenon quickly ③<u>vanished</u>, and people all over the ④<u>world</u> started sending messages.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중, 문맥상 부적절한 것은?

det.korean: 나무 이메일 현상은 빠르게 퍼졌다.
det.analysis: ✅ ①appreciation(고마움): 나무에 대한 '고마움을 표현하는' 메시지. 원문 그대로. ✅ ②low(낮게): 가지가 '낮게' 매달려 있다. 원문 그대로. ❌ ③vanished(사라졌다): 원문은 spread(퍼졌다). 전 세계 사람들이 메시지를 보내기 시작했으므로 현상이 '퍼진' 것. vanished는 정반대. ✅ ④world(세계): 전 '세계'의 사람들. 원문 그대로.
det.tip: spread(퍼지다) ↔ vanish(사라지다). 현상의 확산을 말하는 맥락에서 spread가 적절.

questions.passage: A message that was sent all the way from Russia said, "When I read about this ①<u>wonderful</u> project, I was ②<u>inspired</u> to write to you, even though I live thousands of miles away. Although we are ③<u>connected</u> by a great distance, we share the same ④<u>planet</u> and the same environment."
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중, 문맥상 부적절한 것은?

det.korean: 비록 우리가 엄청난 거리로 떨어져 있기는 하지만.
det.analysis: ✅ ①wonderful(멋진): '멋진' 프로젝트. 원문 그대로. ✅ ②inspired(고무된): 글을 쓰도록 '고무되었다'. 원문 그대로. ❌ ③connected(연결된): 원문은 separated(분리된). 엄청난 거리에 의해 '분리되어' 있다는 맥락. connected(연결된)는 정반대 의미. ✅ ④planet(행성): 같은 '행성'을 공유한다. 원문 그대로.
det.tip: separated by a great distance: 먼 거리로 떨어져 있다. separated ↔ connected.

questions.passage: The story behind these emails begins with Melbourne's Urban Forest Strategy plan, a response to Australia's millennium drought. This drought lasted from the late 1990s to 2010. By the time it ended, 40 percent of the city's 77,000 trees were in a state of declining health.
questions.stem:
다음 글의 내용과 일치하면 T, 일치하지 않으면 F를 고르시오.
"호주의 밀레니엄 가뭄은 2010년 이전에 끝났다."

det.korean: 가뭄은 1990년대 후반부터 2010년까지 계속되었다.
det.analysis: ❌ F: 가뭄은 'from the late 1990s to 2010'으로, 2010년까지 지속되었다. '2010년 이전에 끝났다'는 거짓. 'to 2010'은 2010년까지 포함하므로 2010년 이전에 끝난 것이 아님.
det.tip: 'lasted from A to B'에서 to B는 B까지 포함. '2010년 이전'이 아닌 '2010년까지'.

questions.passage: At first, the "Email this tree" function had a specific purpose. It was designed to allow people to easily inform council workers about trees that were damaged or in poor health.
questions.stem:
다음 글의 내용과 일치하면 T, 일치하지 않으면 F를 고르시오.
"'이 나무에게 이메일 보내기' 기능은 손상되거나 건강이 안 좋은 나무를 보고하기 위해 만들어졌다."

det.korean: 처음에는 손상되거나 건강이 좋지 않은 나무들에 관해 의회 직원들에게 알려주기 위해 고안되었다.
det.analysis: ✅ T: 원문에서 'It was designed to allow people to easily inform council workers about trees that were damaged or in poor health.'라고 명시. 손상/건강 불량 나무 보고가 원래 목적.
det.tip: At first(처음에)가 핵심. 원래 목적(보고)과 실제 사용(편지)이 달라진 점을 구분해야 함.

questions.passage: Meanwhile, the Urban Forest Strategy's tree planting project has remained on track, and canopy cover is predicted to increase from 23 percent in 2012 to 40 percent by the year 2040.
questions.stem:
다음 글의 내용과 일치하면 T, 일치하지 않으면 F를 고르시오.
"2012년 당시 멜버른의 임관 피복도는 40퍼센트였다."

det.korean: 임관 피복도는 2012년의 23퍼센트에서 2040년까지 40퍼센트로 늘어날 것으로 예상된다.
det.analysis: ❌ F: 2012년의 임관 피복도는 23%였고, 40%는 2040년 목표치. 숫자를 뒤바꾼 함정.
det.tip: from 23 percent in 2012 to 40 percent by 2040: 연도와 수치의 대응을 정확히 파악.

questions.passage: As a result, the amount of shade provided by trees within the city, also known as canopy cover, decreased. The loss of canopy cover is a major threat to urban environments because it raises temperatures. Higher temperatures in cities can be dangerous for residents, as they increase the risk of heat exhaustion. They also lead to a rise in the use of air conditioning. This speeds up climate change by increasing energy consumption and greenhouse gas emissions.
questions.stem:
글의 흐름으로 보아 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
"The decrease in canopy cover is harmful because it causes __________"
ch: a decrease in greenhouse gas emissions

det.korean: 임관 피복도의 감소는 기온을 상승시켜 주민에게 위험하기 때문에 해롭다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① higher temperatures that endanger residents
❌ ② more rainfall in urban areas
❌ ③ a decrease in greenhouse gas emissions
❌ ④ lower energy consumption in cities
✅ ①higher temperatures that endanger residents: 원문에서 canopy cover 감소 → 기온 상승 → 주민 위험. ✗ ②more rainfall: 강수량 언급 없음. ✗ ③a decrease in greenhouse gas emissions: 오히려 배출 증가. ✗ ④lower energy consumption: 에어컨 사용 증가로 에너지 소비 증가.
det.tip: 인과관계: canopy cover 감소 → 기온 상승 → 열사병 위험 증가 + 에어컨 사용 증가 → 기후변화 가속화.

questions.passage: The global popularity of the tree mail phenomenon reminds us that we are all connected to nature, and we are all involved in building a more sustainable world. Without collective action from people across the globe, we would have little hope of saving our planet for future generations. Locally, the tree mail phenomenon has inspired many Melbourne residents to offer their own ideas about building an environmentally friendly urban environment. Some have even volunteered to measure trees and monitor animals for nature programs in the city.
questions.stem:
글의 흐름으로 보아 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
"The tree mail phenomenon shows that __________"
ch: technology is the key to solving environmental issues
individual efforts are more important than group action
saving the planet requires cooperation from everyone
trees can communicate with humans through email

det.korean: 나무 이메일 현상은 지구를 구하려면 모두의 협력이 필요하다는 것을 보여준다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① technology is the key to solving environmental issues
❌ ② individual efforts are more important than group action
✅ ③ saving the planet requires cooperation from everyone
❌ ④ trees can communicate with humans through email
✅ ③saving the planet requires cooperation from everyone: 'collective action from people across the globe'가 핵심. 전 세계적 협력 없이는 희망이 없다. ✗ ①기술이 핵심: 기술 언급 없음. ✗ ②개인 노력이 더 중요: collective(집단적) 행동을 강조. ✗ ④나무가 이메일로 소통: 비유적 표현을 문자 그대로 해석한 오답.
det.tip: collective action(집단 행동)이 핵심 메시지. 개인이 아닌 전 세계적 협력을 강조.

questions.passage: Something had to be done to deal with the loss of Melbourne's trees. In 2012, the city government announced its Urban Forest Strategy plan. It set the ambitious goal of planting more than 3,000 trees every year for the next twenty years. The plan also involved the creation of an online map called the Urban Forest Visual.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
ch: The Urban Forest Strategy was announced before 2010.
The plan aimed to plant over 3,000 trees annually for 20 years.
The online map was called the Urban Forest Strategy.
The city planned to plant exactly 3,000 trees each year.

det.korean: 그 계획은 다음 20년 동안 매년 3,000그루가 넘는 나무를 심는 목표를 설정했다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① The Urban Forest Strategy was announced before 2010.
✅ ② The plan aimed to plant over 3,000 trees annually for 20 yea
❌ ③ The online map was called the Urban Forest Strategy.
❌ ④ The city planned to plant exactly 3,000 trees each year.
✅ ②20년간 매년 3,000그루 이상: 'more than 3,000 trees every year for the next twenty years'. ✗ ①2010년 이전 발표: 2012년에 발표. ✗ ③지도 이름이 Urban Forest Strategy: 지도 이름은 Urban Forest Visual. ✗ ④정확히 3,000그루: 'more than 3,000'이므로 3,000 초과.
det.tip: 'more than 3,000'은 '3,000 초과'. 'exactly 3,000'과 구별해야 함.

questions.passage: This interactive map shows the location of every single tree in the city's parks and along its roads. It uses colors and symbols to indicate each tree's age and genus. Also, users can click on a tree to find out its species and even send it an email.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
ch: The map only shows trees in city parks, not along roads.
The map uses colors to show the tree's species directly.
Users cannot interact with individual trees on the map.
Users can learn a tree's species by clicking on it.

det.korean: 사용자들은 나무를 클릭하여 그것의 종을 알아낼 수 있다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① The map only shows trees in city parks, not along roads.
❌ ② The map uses colors to show the tree's species directly.
❌ ③ Users cannot interact with individual trees on the map.
✅ ④ Users can learn a tree's species by clicking on it.
✅ ④나무 클릭으로 종을 알 수 있다: 'click on a tree to find out its species'. ✗ ①공원만 보여줌: 'parks and along its roads' 둘 다. ✗ ②색상이 종을 직접 표시: 색상과 기호는 age와 genus를 나타냄. species는 클릭해야 알 수 있음. ✗ ③개별 나무와 상호작용 불가: 클릭해서 정보를 얻고 이메일을 보낼 수 있음.
det.tip: genus(속) vs species(종): 색상·기호로 표시되는 것은 age와 genus. species는 클릭 필요.

questions.passage: ① Locally, the tree mail phenomenon has inspired many Melbourne residents to offer their own ideas about building an environmentally friendly urban environment. ② Some have even volunteered to measure trees and monitor animals for nature programs in the city. ③ Meanwhile, the Urban Forest Strategy's tree planting project has fallen behind schedule. ④ Canopy cover is predicted to increase from 23 percent in 2012 to 40 percent by the year 2040.
questions.stem: 다음 글에서 원문과 다르게 바뀐 문장은?

det.korean: 한편, 도시숲 전략의 나무 심기 프로젝트는 계속 진행 중이다.
det.analysis: ✅ ①②④: 원문 그대로. ❌ ③: 원문은 'has remained on track(계획대로 진행 중)'. 'has fallen behind schedule(일정에 뒤처졌다)'로 바뀌어 정반대 의미.
det.tip: remain on track(계획대로 진행되다) ↔ fall behind schedule(일정에 뒤처지다).

questions.passage: The loss of canopy cover is a major threat to urban environments because it raises temperatures. Higher temperatures in cities can be dangerous for residents, as they increase the risk of heat exhaustion. They also lead to a rise in the use of air conditioning. This speeds up climate change by increasing __________ and __________. Something had to be done to deal with the loss of Melbourne's trees.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 두 빈칸에 들어갈 영어 표현을 순서대로 쓰시오. (and로 연결)
questions.wa: energy consumption and greenhouse gas emissions
accept: energy consumption and greenhouse gas emissions
Energy consumption and greenhouse gas emissions

det.korean: 에너지 소비와 온실가스 배출물을 증가시킴으로써.
det.analysis: 원문: 'by increasing energy consumption and greenhouse gas emissions'. 에어컨 사용 → 에너지 소비 + 온실가스 배출 증가 → 기후변화 가속화.
det.tip: energy consumption(에너지 소비)과 greenhouse gas emissions(온실가스 배출): 기후변화의 두 가지 핵심 원인.

questions.ans: energy consumption and greenhouse gas emissions

questions.passage: After the map was posted online, something unexpected happened. The trees started receiving thousands of emails, but many of them were not reports about damage or poor health. Instead, they were love letters, poems, greetings, and messages expressing appreciation for the trees.
questions.stem: 사람들이 나무에게 보낸 이메일의 내용을 4가지 본문의 영어 단어로 쓰시오. (쉼표로 구분)
accept: love letters, poems, greetings, and messages

det.korean: 연애편지, 시, 인사말, 그리고 메시지들.
det.analysis: 원문: 'they were love letters, poems, greetings, and messages expressing appreciation for the trees.' 4가지 유형을 나열.
det.tip: 나열형 서술형: 원문에서 정확한 단어를 추출하는 것이 핵심.

questions.passage: In 2012, the city government announced its Urban Forest Strategy plan. It __________. The plan also involved the creation of an online map called the Urban Forest Visual.
questions.stem:
다음 주어진 단어를 올바른 순서로 배열하시오.
[ the / of / ambitious / set / goal / planting / more than 3,000 trees / every year / for the next twenty years ]
questions.wa: set the ambitious goal of planting more than 3,000 trees every year for the next twenty years
accept: SET THE AMBITIOUS GOAL OF PLANTING MORE THAN 3,000 TREES EVERY YEAR FOR THE NEXT TWENTY YEARS
Set the ambitious goal of planting more than 3,000 trees every year for the next twenty years
set the ambitious goal of planting more than 3,000 trees every year for the next twenty years

det.korean: 다음 20년 동안 매년 3,000그루가 넘는 나무를 심는 야심찬 목표를 설정했다.
det.analysis: 원문: 'It set the ambitious goal of planting more than 3,000 trees every year for the next twenty years.' set + the ambitious goal + of planting 구조.
det.tip: set the goal of V-ing: ~하는 목표를 설정하다. 'of + 동명사'로 목표의 내용을 설명.

questions.ans: set the ambitious goal of planting more than 3,000 trees every year for the next twenty years

questions.passage: The global popularity of the tree mail phenomenon reminds us that we are all connected to nature, and we are all involved in building a more sustainable world. Without collective action from people across the globe, we would have little hope of saving our planet for future generations. Locally, the tree mail phenomenon has inspired many Melbourne residents to offer their own ideas about building an environmentally friendly urban environment.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: the history of email technology in Australia
how trees in Melbourne were damaged by drought
the economic benefits of planting urban trees
the importance of collective action for a sustainable future

det.korean: 나무 이메일 현상은 지속 가능한 미래를 위한 집단 행동의 중요성을 일깨워 준다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① the history of email technology in Australia
❌ ② how trees in Melbourne were damaged by drought
❌ ③ the economic benefits of planting urban trees
✅ ④ the importance of collective action for a sustainable future
✅ ④지속 가능한 미래를 위한 집단 행동: 'collective action', 'sustainable world', 'connected to nature'가 핵심. ✗ ①이메일 기술의 역사: 기술 자체가 아닌 환경 메시지가 핵심. ✗ ②가뭄 피해: 배경이지 주제가 아님. ✗ ③경제적 이익: 경제 언급 없음.
det.tip: 주제 파악: 마지막 단락의 핵심 메시지(collective action, sustainable world)에 주목.

questions.passage: Melbourne's Urban Forest Strategy plan was created in response to the millennium drought, which damaged many of the city's trees and reduced canopy cover. The plan involved planting thousands of trees and creating an interactive online map.
questions.stem:
다음 글을 한 문장으로 요약할 때, 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
"Melbourne's tree planting strategy not only addressed environmental damage but also __________ between people and nature."

det.korean: 멜버른의 나무 심기 전략은 환경 피해에 대처했을 뿐 아니라 사람과 자연 사이의 연결을 강화했다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① created conflict
✅ ② strengthened the connection
❌ ③ weakened the relationship
❌ ④ eliminated the gap
✅ ②strengthened the connection(연결을 강화했다): 나무 이메일 현상이 사람과 자연의 연결을 보여주고, 주민 참여를 고무. ✗ ①갈등 생성: 긍정적 결과와 반대. ✗ ③관계 약화: 정반대. ✗ ④격차 제거: 과장된 표현.
det.tip: 요약 문제: 글 전체의 긍정적 결과(환경 복구 + 인간-자연 연결)를 하나로 압축.

questions.stem:
다음 한국어를 영어로 옮기시오.
"전 세계 사람들로부터의 집단적인 행동이 없다면, 우리는 미래의 세대들을 위해 우리의 지구를 구할 희망을 거의 갖지 못할 것이다."
questions.wa: Without collective action from people across the globe, we would have little hope of saving our planet for future generations.
accept: WITHOUT COLLECTIVE ACTION FROM PEOPLE ACROSS THE GLOBE, WE WOULD HAVE LITTLE HOPE OF SAVING OUR PLANET FOR FUTURE GENERATIONS.
Without collective action from people across the globe we would have little hope of saving our planet for future generations
Without collective action from people across the globe, we would have little hope of saving our planet for future generations

det.korean: 원문 직역 영작 문제.
det.analysis: 핵심 구문: Without + 명사, S + would + V (가정법 과거). collective action(집단적 행동), across the globe(전 세계), little hope of V-ing(~할 희망이 거의 없다).
det.tip: Without ~, S would V: '~이 없다면, ~할 것이다' 가정법 과거 구문. little = almost no(거의 없는).

questions.ans: Without collective action from people across the globe, we would have little hope of saving our planet for future generations.
